slides.title: What you need to earn to rent alone
slides.sub: Median one-bedroom rent in the U.S.: $1,215 a month.

slides.heading: The 30% rule
body: Housing is generally considered affordable if it costs no more than 30% of your income. Pay more and you're "cost-burdened."
Flip it around: your yearly income should be about 40 times your monthly rent.

slides.heading: The math at $1,215
body: $1,215 a month is $14,580 a year in rent. At 30%, you'd need about $48,600 a year before taxes.
Working full time (2,080 hours), that's about $23.37 an hour.

slides.heading: On a first-job paycheck
body: A full-time cashier at the $15.81 median earns about $32,900 a year. 30% of that is about $822 a month for rent.
Splitting a place with a roommate is one way to get your share under that.
slides.source: BLS cashier pay, May 2025; HFLIC calculation

slides.takeaway: Before you sign a lease, run the 30% math on the real rent near you.

posts.caption:
Moving out after graduation? The median one-bedroom rent in the U.S. was $1,215 a month in October 2026 (Apartment List).

The usual rule: housing is considered affordable if it costs no more than 30% of your income. That means earning about 40 times your monthly rent each year. For $1,215, that's about $48,600 a year before taxes, or about $23.37 an hour working full time.

Compare that with a first job: a full-time cashier at the $15.81 median earns about $32,900 a year, so 30% is about $822 a month. A roommate is one way to close the gap. Rents vary a lot by city, so run the math on real listings near you.

Data: Apartment List national rent report (October 2026, via CRE Daily); Congressional Research Service (Aug. 2026); BLS cashier pay (May 2025).
